territorial_scope.description: Applies within Virginia to the utility's rates and terms, as an order in a single proceeding directed at Dominion under Virginia's Code.

evidence.quote: pursuant to § 56-585.1 A of the Code of Virginia

summary.short: Final order of Virginia's State Corporation Commission setting Dominion's base rates for 2026 and 2027 and approving a new GS-5 rate class for large-load customers, including data centers, with contract, collateral and minimum-demand terms effective from January 1, 2027.
summary.long: Final order of the Virginia State Corporation Commission in Case PUR-2025-00058 setting Virginia Electric and Power Company's (Dominion) base rates for 2026 and 2027 under Va. Code § 56-585.1 A. It approves base-rate revenue increases of $565.7 million for 2026 and $209.9 million for 2027, a 9.8% return on equity within a 9.3%–10.3% range, and Staff's capital structure. It creates Rate Schedule GS-5, effective January 1, 2027, for customers with 25 MW or more of demand on a contiguous site and a load factor of at least 75%. For contracts signed from that date, the order sets a 14-year term, collateral of $1.5 million per MW with reductions up to 70%, minimum demand charges (85% distribution and transmission, 60% generation), exit fees and capacity-reduction rules. Other directives cover demand-side management and data-center expenditure forecasts, cost-allocation studies moving away from the average-and-excess method, reporting on Rate Schedules MBR and SCR, and a large-load interconnection queue filing due February 2, 2026. Estimated residential bills rise $11.24 (7.5%) in 2026 and $2.36 (1.5%) in 2027.

Code § 56-249.6 in footnote 1 (p. 1); both are recorded as stated. The order cites several subsections of Code § 56-585.1 (A 2 a, A 4, A 6, A 7, A 8 e, A 11), recorded as one legal-basis row because the target is the same section. Target instrument IDs are empty because no registry match was supplied for the Code sections or court decisions. The GS-5 rate class shall include customers with: (1) a measured or contracted demand of 25 megawatts (“MW”) or greater on a contiguous site; and (2) a measured or expected load factor of at least 75%.
Rate Schedule MBR is an experimental rate structured to reflect market-based rate pricing in the PJM wholesale market.
Rate Schedule SCR is a market-based pricing rate that is similar to MBR but only open to customers who are party to the SCR contract.

enforcement.note: Rate-setting final order; it creates no fines, penalties, licence revocations, clawbacks, suspensions or blocking regimes. The only related item is a contract exit fee for customers that cease operations or default during the GS-5 contract term (Contract section, footnote 97), a charge under the customer agreement rather than a sanction imposed by the Commission, so it is not coded here.
